title: Les Dissonances: Cross-Tool Harvesting and Polluting in Pool-of-Tools Empowered LLM Agents
pdf_path: papers/Les Dissonances_Cross-Tool Harvesting and Polluting in Pool-of-Tools Empowered LLM Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: A malicious tool in a pool of tools parasitically attaches to a victim tool via semantic or format dependencies, hijacks the agent's task control flow, then harvests or pollutes data across tools. No cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: First systematic analysis of task control flow in pool-of-tools agents
XTHP attack: cross-tool harvesting and polluting via parasitic tool dependencies
Measurement of 66 real tools: 75% hijackable, 72% harvestable, 68% pollutable
Chord automated scanner and evaluation against existing defenses
limitations: Pre-configured LangChain/Llama-Index tools rather than arbitrary marketplaces
Defense evaluation limited to existing LLM/planning defenses
theoretical_crypto_links: None; no cryptographic construction or proof
Task-bound capability tokens and signed tool manifests are our inference only
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, MACs, credentials, TEE or ZK
Signing tool descriptions does not prevent semantic parasitism (our inference)

title: ObliInjection: Order-Oblivious Prompt Injection Attack to LLM Agents with Multi-source Data
pdf_path: papers/ObliInjection_Order-Oblivious Prompt Injection Attack to LLM Agents with Multi-source Data.pdf
threat_model_summary: Attacker controls one or a few data segments among many sources; the agent assembles them in an unknown order. Goal: make the agent follow the injected task regardless of segment ordering, measured in expectation over sampled permutations rather than worst-case.
core_contributions: First single-segment prompt injection attack for multi-source agents
Order-oblivious loss defined as expected cross-entropy over random permutations
99.0%/98.7%/99.6% average ASR on Amazon Reviews/Multi-News/HotpotQA
Evaluation of transfer, black-box settings and existing defenses
limitations: Order-oblivious is expectation over sampled orders, not a worst-case guarantee
Requires optimizing against a shadow model and sampling permutations
Defense evaluation limited; StruQ/SecAlign still vulnerable
Internal inconsistencies reported in the note
theoretical_crypto_links: None; 'order-oblivious' is an optimization expectation, not ORAM or order-oblivious encryption
Authenticated provenance is orthogonal to semantic injection (our inference)
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, commitments, ZK, MPC or TEE
Segment commitments/logs only support audit, not prevention (our inference)

title: Attention is All You Need to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs
pdf_path: papers/Attention is All You Need to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs.pdf
threat_model_summary: Indirect prompt injection in external data processed by an LLM-integrated application. The defense assumes white-box access to attention maps and trains a token-level detector; adaptive attackers may evade it. No cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: RENNERVATE: attention-based token-level IPI detector and sanitizer
Two-level attentive pooling over heads and response tokens
FIPI dataset of 100k injected and 10k benign samples
99.58% detection accuracy and near-zero ASR across five open LLMs
limitations: Detection threshold and contiguous-span heuristic are empirical
theoretical_crypto_links: None; attention weights are not authentication
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, TEE or credentials
Source authentication is at most peripheral (our inference)

title: Autonomy Comes with Costs: Detecting Denial-of-Service Vulnerabilities Caused by Resource Abusing in LLM-based Agents
pdf_path: papers/Autonomy Comes with Costs_Detecting Denial-of-Service Vulnerabilities Caused by Resource Abusing in LLM-based Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Grey-box attacker can inspect agent source code and induce resource exhaustion through memory/disk lifecycle bugs; single-turn, same-session and cross-session resource retention. No cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: First resource-management security study of LLM-based agents
Resource lifecycle taxonomy: short-lived, long-lived, full-lifecycle
AgentDoS: CodeQL static analysis plus LLM-generated and scheduled fuzzing
36 zero-days across 16 agents and 15 CVEs; 100% precision
limitations: Requires source code; not applicable to closed GPTs/Coze
Time/size thresholds may miss slow accumulation
theoretical_crypto_links: None; resource monitoring and fuzzing are not cryptographic
Verifiable metering and attestation are our inference and do not stop authorized exhaustion
applied_crypto_links: Docker memory/disk limits are test-environment constraints, not security budgets

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
pdf_path: papers/Agent Security Bench (ASB)_Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Benchmark models attackers at four agent stages (system prompt, user prompt, memory retrieval, tool call); covers direct/indirect prompt injection, memory poisoning, Plan-of-Thought backdoor and mixed attacks. Not a cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: Unified benchmark for agent attacks and defenses
10 scenarios, 10 agents, 50 normal tasks, 400 attack tasks, 420 tools, 13 LLM backbones
Formalized attack objectives and NRP utility-security metric
Systematic defense evaluation showing prompt-level defenses are largely ineffective
limitations: 'Formalizing' is indicator-function notation, not a security definition
Benchmark scope limited to selected scenarios/tools
Internal numerical inconsistencies reported in the note
theoretical_crypto_links: None; no security game, theorem or reduction
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
